lines: An oscillator giving sine, triangle, sawtooth and pulse from one phase at the same time, with a white noise source beside them, and frequency, amplitude and pulse width modulation inputs
Sets the frequency, five octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the duty cycle of the SQR output, an even square at the centre and a narrowing pulse towards either end; the other four outputs take no notice of it
Attenuates and inverts the pulse width modulation voltage before it shifts the duty cycle of the SQR output, and at the centre that voltage changes nothing
Scales the frequency modulation voltage, 5V moving the frequency by 261.63Hz at the clockwise end; turned counter-clockwise past the centre it inverts the modulation
Sets how far the amplitude modulation voltage controls the level, from no effect at the counter-clockwise end to the voltage setting the level outright at the clockwise end
Transposes the oscillator at one volt per octave, added to the FREQ knob
Shifts the duty cycle of the SQR output, 10V moving it by half the full width at the clockwise end of its attenuverter, and the result is held between 1% and 99%
Modulates the frequency, scaled by the FM knob; the shift is added to the frequency rather than multiplied by it, so a large enough negative voltage runs the oscillator backwards
Resets the oscillator's phase to zero on each rising edge past 1V, which is hard sync, and the SYNC lamp flashes for 0.15 seconds each time
Sets the level of the SIN, TRI, SAW and SQR outputs, scaled by the AM knob, with 10V full and 0V silent at the clockwise end of that knob; the NOIS output is left alone
A triangle wave at ±5V, its two corners rounded by polyBLAMP so they do not alias
A sawtooth wave at ±5V, its step smoothed by polyBLEP so it does not alias
A pulse wave at ±5V whose duty cycle comes from the PW knob and the pulse width modulation input, with both its edges smoothed by polyBLEP
White noise at ±5V, a fresh random value every sample, unrelated to the oscillator's frequency and phase and untouched by the amplitude modulation
Note — the four oscillator waveforms come from a single phase, so they are always at the same frequency and all restart together at a sync pulse
Note — a waveform is worked out only while something is patched into its output, so outputs left empty cost no processing
Note — the FM lamp brightens with the frequency modulation voltage multiplied by the depth set on the FM knob, and stays dark while the FM jack is empty

0.why: Wavemaker.cpp:98 reads getVoltage() with no channel and adds it to the knob as an octave exponent at line 99, with no clamp on either side

1.why: Wavemaker.cpp:198-202 divides getVoltage() with no channel by 10, scales it by the modulation knob and by a half, adds it to the PW knob and clamps the sum to 0.01 and 0.99

2.why: Wavemaker.cpp:105-106 reads getVoltage() with no channel, multiplies it by the FM knob and by 261.63 over 5, and adds the result to the frequency with no clamp

3.why: Wavemaker.cpp:123 passes getVoltage() with no channel to a dsp::SchmittTrigger with thresholds of 0.1 and 1

4.normal: full level, the modulation switched off
4.why: Wavemaker.cpp:140-146 tests isConnected and then divides getVoltage() with no channel by 10 and mixes it against 1 by the AM knob, with no clamp, so a negative voltage inverts the waveform

0.why: Wavemaker.cpp:161 writes one sine value scaled by 5 with setVoltage; the module never calls setChannels and the binary imports no such symbol

1.why: Wavemaker.cpp:178 writes one triangle value scaled by 5 with setVoltage

2.why: Wavemaker.cpp:188 writes one sawtooth value scaled by 5 with setVoltage

3.why: Wavemaker.cpp:215 writes one square value scaled by 5 with setVoltage

4.why: Wavemaker.cpp:222 writes random::uniform() mapped to -1 and 1 and scaled by 5, outside the block that applies the amplitude modulation

Wavemaker.notes: Read at commit dc4aa7f, the repository head; cf19c15 first carried the installed 2.1.0 and the two commits after it change only plugin.json, so the source is the same either way. The maker's user manual says the amplitude modulation is applied equally to all generated waveforms, and the code applies it to the sine, triangle, sawtooth and square only, leaving the noise output at full level; the lines say so. The manual calls the duty cycle control the PWM knob and the panel prints PW. The panel prints no name at all on the pulse width modulation knob or its jack, only a line joining them to PW. The PW knob's own range runs from 0.1% to 99.9%, but the square wave clamps the total to 1% and 99%, so the last of the knob's travel at each end makes no difference. The module has no context menu of its own. Nothing here is polyphonic: every jack is read with getVoltage() and no channel, and the binary imports neither setChannels nor getPolyVoltage.
